open_items.title: Objects the wheel's text does not name: which terms govern
technical_evidence: The wheels carry the CUDA EULA with the supplement 'Release date: August 16, 2018'; its Attachment A lists neither libnvJitLink.so nor libcufile.so and the text does not name NVSHMEM (checked per object, bundled_texts).

The CUDA 13.0 Update 2 EULA (archive page, 'Last updated: January 7, 2025') lists libnvJitLink.so and libcufile.so in Attachment A; the 13.0.2 release notes' component table gives exactly these wheels' versions (official_terms).
The NVSHMEM 3.4.5 SLA makes 'any portion of the SDK' distributable; the CUDA 13.0.2 EULA does not list libnvshmem.

The package now ships both: each wheel's License.txt and the version-matched official text under licenses/terms/ (cuda_eula_13.0.2.txt, nvshmem_sla_3.4.5.txt), each re-derived from its snapshot by the checker.
licence_interpretation: The 2018 text in the wheel does not by its own words grant distribution of these three objects; the version-matched official terms do.
Shipping the official text records what the grant rests on; it does not make that text the governing one.
legal_uncertainty: Which text governs an object received as a PyPI wheel whose own licence file is older than, and narrower than, the toolkit release the object belongs to.
Whether NVSHMEM received inside a wheel that carries the CUDA EULA is under the NVSHMEM SLA at all.

open_items.title: cuDNN and TensorRT: two texts, downstream terms, licence term
technical_evidence: cuDNN: the wheel's supplement names 'the runtime files .so and .h, cudnn64_7.dll, and cudnn.lib'; the 9.19.0 documentation's names 'the runtime files .so and .dll'. Both texts ship (licenses/nvidia_cudnn_cu13-9.19.0.56/, licenses/terms/cudnn_sla_9.19.0.txt).

TensorRT: the wheel's LICENSE.txt is the NVIDIA Software License Agreement with the TensorRT Supplement; the 10.16.1 documentation is the SDK agreement. Both ship (licenses/tensorrt_cu12_libs-10.16.1.11/, licenses/terms/tensorrt_sla_10.16.1.txt).

TensorRT wheel §12.2: an initial one-year term from delivery or download, renewing automatically for one-year periods; NVIDIA may terminate on 90 days' written notice before a renewal year. The Supplement adds that expiry or termination does not affect rights already granted to compliant recipients.

TensorRT wheel Supplement: distribution only in binary form, as a component of a product with additional material functionality, and 'you shall require in your agreements with your Customers that their distributions be on terms at least as restrictive'.
A downstream-terms draft with per-clause scope is rendered to shipping/DOWNSTREAM_TERMS.draft.md (downstream_terms). It is not in the package and is not in force.
licence_interpretation: Both cuDNN texts and both TensorRT texts grant distribution of the shipped .so files.
The TensorRT wheel text requires an agreement with each Customer; a README or THIRD_PARTY.md statement in the package is not an agreement and does not by itself meet that requirement.
legal_uncertainty: Which cuDNN and which TensorRT text governs the wheels as received.
What form of 'agreement with your Customers' is required for a free download (click-through, licence file, release terms), and whether the draft's clauses are 'at least as restrictive'.
How a one-year, renewable licence term interacts with copies already distributed, beyond the Supplement's sentence on recipients' rights.
Whether the wheel SLA §2 (iii)(d) bar on making the software available 'by means of the internet' limits an internet download of the package despite the Supplement's distribution grant.

open_items.title: libgomp: GPLv3 corresponding source
technical_evidence: Shipped libgomp.so.1 (sha256 e28fb289...) and AlmaLinux's libgomp-8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1 /usr/lib64/libgomp.so.1.0.0 (sha256 e985bcbb...) have the same build ID and byte-identical code and data sections; they differ only in the DT_RPATH the wheel's build added (corresponding_source.correspondence; license_audit.py corresponding-source re-checks this).
The binary package's RPM header names SOURCERPM gcc-8.5.0-28.el8_10.alma.1.src.rpm; both packages' sha256 are in AlmaLinux's signed repository metadata (corresponding_source.authentication).

COPYING3 and COPYING.RUNTIME ship under licenses/libgomp/, byte-identical to the members of the source package's gcc-8.5.0-20210514.tar.xz. COPYING3 differs from gnu.org's current gpl-3.0.txt only in four http -> https URLs.
licenses/libgomp/SOURCE.txt names the source package, its sha256 and where to get it. The source package is not yet published next to any package (local-only).
The correspondence is shown by comparing binaries, not by rebuilding: the source package was not rebuilt to reproduce the bytes.
licence_interpretation: GPLv3 §6(d) lets object code offered from a network server point to the Corresponding Source on another server with clear directions, while the distributor stays obligated to keep it available; publishing the source package next to the package (corresponding_source.mirror) is the arrangement chosen.
The GCC Runtime Library Exception covers Target Code combined with the Runtime Library; libgomp itself remains under GPLv3.
legal_uncertainty: Whether the source package plus the comparison above is the 'Corresponding Source' of an object whose dynamic tables a third party's tool rewrote (and whether that tool step must be included).
Whether the Runtime Library Exception's 'Eligible Compilation Process' condition holds for this process image, where NVIDIA objects not compiled by GCC and not linking libgomp are loaded next to it.
How long the source must stay available, and whether a release file next to the package meets §6(d) for every channel the owner may choose.

open_items.title: NVIDIA's common distribution conditions
technical_evidence: Material additional functionality: saccade_track is the whole MOT pipeline; about 20,700 lines of Saccade-authored C++/CUDA are compiled into the entrypoint and the operator library. The package has no headers, CMake config or pkg-config for third parties (check_shipping_bundle.py layout_exact), and lib/vendor/ is exactly the set the PR-12 run loaded.

Access: only Saccade's own objects load lib/vendor/ (the entrypoint via DT_NEEDED, the operator library via dlopen). The launcher's --library-path and rtld-audit check constrain where saccade_track loads from; they do not stop other programs from loading lib/vendor/ (files 0644/0755, SONAMEs and symbols intact, readable by any local user).
The model and engine sha256 come from the --lineage / --attestation JSON the user passes; the entrypoint has no compiled-in hash, so a user can point it at another I/O-compatible engine.

Open-source licences: Saccade is Apache-2.0 and README.txt / THIRD_PARTY.md exclude lib/vendor/ from it; no NVIDIA object links libgomp (only libtorch_cpu.so and libtorch_nvshmem.so do). The model root ships a YOLO26s-derived engine whose upstream licence position is AGPL-3.0 (ADR 023; open item M-1).
Full audit: results/547_l4_audit/20261008T125352Z/audit.md.
licence_interpretation: On their words, the tracker pipeline is functionality beyond the SDK, and Apache-2.0 alone does not subject the SDK to an open-source licence.

'Only accessed by your application' can be read as a design and distribution duty (do not expose or offer the libraries for other programs) or as technical exclusivity; the package meets the first in what it ships and says, not the second. --library-path is not proof of either.
legal_uncertainty: What 'material' requires, and whether objects only loaded as LibTorch dependencies count as incorporated into the application.
Which reading of 'only accessed by your application' applies, and whether downstream terms restricting lib/vendor/ to saccade_track are needed.
Whether the AGPL position on the bundled YOLO26 lineage (M-1) would subject the SDK to an open-source licence.

open_items.title: Model root licences (outside lib/vendor/)
open_items.scope: share/saccade/models/ (yolo26s_backbone_640_best.engine, the Mamba head TorchScript and its lineage)
technical_evidence: The backbone engine is a MOT17-fine-tuned Ultralytics YOLO26s (docs/modules/detection/mamba-head-training.md); the Mamba head was trained with ultralytics' v8DetectionLoss and a YOLO teacher.
This audit covers lib/vendor/ only; no licence text or notice in the package covers the model root.
The training data's terms (MOT17 and others) were not retrieved or checked.
Model/runtime separation is tracked separately (#549); it changes no licence status here.
licence_interpretation: ADR 023 records that upstream places YOLO code, architecture and models trained with its pipeline under AGPL-3.0 by default, and that compiling to a TensorRT engine does not by itself remove that lineage.
legal_uncertainty: Whether the shipped engine and head are subject to AGPL-3.0 (commercial licence, legal opinion, or a different backbone are the owner's options).
Whether the training data's terms allow distributing weights trained on it.

downstream_terms.reading: A draft of the terms a recipient would accept for the NVIDIA components, for the owner and counsel. Not in force, not in the package, and not an agreement: shipping it, or a README statement, does not by itself meet a requirement to have agreements with Customers. Each clause names the objects it applies to and the quoted terms it rests on, and each quote is checked in the wheel licence text of every object it is cited for; nothing here applies to Saccade's own code (Apache-2.0), PyTorch (BSD-3-Clause), NCCL (BSD-3-Clause) or libgomp (GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1), whose licences forbid or do not need further restrictions.
